title: Three ways to average a bag of odds

data.source: Csiszar (1975), Karcher (1977), Amari and Nagaoka (2000), Banerjee et al. (2005); cited from memory. Computed on the worked family of Phoenix_Egg/CORE/MATHEMATICS.md section I, seeded.

prediction: Averaged in mixture coordinates or in exponential coordinates, the seed obeys Amari's Pythagorean identity exactly; the literal Fisher-Rao Frechet seed obeys neither and is a third, different distribution; the flat recursion equals its batch mean in the two flat coordinates and not on the Fisher-Rao sphere.
baseline: Amari's dually flat geometry and the generalised Pythagorean theorem (Csiszar 1975; Amari and Nagaoka 2000); Bregman centroids (Banerjee et al. 2005); the Karcher mean (1977). Decoy: the renormalised median.
relation: a special case once a coordinate is chosen; the literal Frechet mean is neither projection
status_line: CRR here is: a special case of Amari's two flat means once a coordinate is chosen, which R5 does not do; its literal Frechet seed is neither projection but the known Karcher mean.
why: R5 (Phoenix status ASSUMPTION) gives a flat recursion without naming the flat coordinate. In mixture coordinates the seed is the mean that satisfies Amari's Pythagorean identity for one relative entropy; in exponential coordinates it satisfies the mirror identity; both to rounding error. The literal Frechet mean with the Fisher-Rao distance is a third distribution that satisfies neither, and its recursion differs from its batch form on a curved family, as R5 itself says. So the question 'which projection is the seed?' has three answers, and R5 leaves the choice open.
